title: API-credential-usage-cards UX proposals and backlog
content:
Summary:

This doc collects UX proposals, quick wireframe notes, and a groomed backlog for a new console surface that shows API-credential (key-level) and route-level usage and limits. The goal is a compact ‘usage card’ view that can be embedded on the keys list, on a per-API-key detail page, and as a per-route summary in the Routes table.

Design goals / constraints:
- Make it easy to answer: Is this key about to hit its quota? Which routes are driving cost and token consumption?
- Scannable and compact: cards should be readable at a glance in a list of keys (4–6 cards per row depending on screen width).
- Progressive disclosure: summary + expand for history and allocation controls (throttles, soft/hard limits).
- Support multiple quota models: token-based, request-count, embedding-units, and composite (e.g., token + requests).
- Respect roles: admins see global quotas + per-key, devs see only their keys.

Primary personas:
- Platform engineer (SRE): wants quick view of keys nearing capacity and ability to add temporary burst or reroute traffic.
- App engineer: wants to understand which route (e.g., /chat vs /embeddings) is costing most tokens under their key.
- Finance ops: wants rollup metrics and exportable CSV of usage by billing tag.

Key interactions described:
1) Key list card (compact) — default state (90% of users):
   - Header: key name (redacted), tier badge (dev/prod/dedicated), last-used timestamp
   - Prominent metric: percent of monthly quota used (large progress ring with numeric percent inside)
   - Secondary metrics (inline): 24h token delta, avg latency for top route, estimated burn rate (tokens/day)
   - Quick actions: ‘View details’, ‘Throttle’, ‘Revoke’

2) Key expanded panel (on click or vertical drawer):
   - Time-series sparkline (30d) showing tokens consumed with annotations for rollouts/canary toggles
   - Top 3 routes by token consumption (sortable) with mini bars and % contribution
   - Recent anomalous spikes (auto-detected) with one-click to open trace in Observability
   - Allocation controls: soft-limit slider, hard-limit toggle, burst allowance dropdown
   - Explainers: how billing maps to tokens vs requests, and what a throttle will do to responses

3) Route-level row augmentation (Routes table):
   - Small badge with percent of parent key’s usage + color-coded impact (green/yellow/red)
   - Click opens route breakdown modal showing per-key contribution, per-model breakdown (if available), and suggestions for lower-cost model/quantization

Wireframe notes (rough ASCII):
[Key list - desktop card]
+-------------------------------------------------+
| Key: redacted-key-2        [dev]   last used 2h |
|  (progress ring 67%)  67% of monthly quota used |
|  24h: +4.2k tokens  |  Avg latency: 210ms | ~3k t/day |
|  [View details] [Throttle] [Revoke]             |
+-------------------------------------------------+

Accessibility/visual rules:
- Progress ring must have text alternative (percent + aria-label: tokens used / tokens quota).
- Color should not be the only indicator of severity — add an icon + label.
- Use condensed type for numeric rows to keep cards small.

Data model and back-end notes (consumer-facing summary):
- The card surface reads a small, pre-aggregated payload: current_quota, used_tokens_month, last_24h_delta, top_routes (name + tokens), burn_rate_estimate.
- Endpoint should be optimized for list render (batched request for up to 50 keys).
- Fallback: if route-level breakdown not available (older logs), show ‘route breakdown delayed — last updated Xh ago’.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- [M] List view shows progress ring, percent, and last-24h delta for each key.
- [M] Clicking a card expands details with a 30d sparkline and top 3 routes.
- [M] Throttle control in expanded view can set a soft-limit and persists to backend (audit log entry created).
- [S] Route rows show per-key percent-of-key usage badge.
- [S] CSV export of keys list with chosen date range.
- [B] Integrate anomaly list items with Observability traces (link only — no cross-products integration in MVP).

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Quota window semantics: calendar-month vs rolling-30d? Default should be calendar-month for billing clarity; allow toggle for rolling.
- Do we allow per-route hard limits or only key-level hard limits? Proposal: start with key-level only, surface per-route suggestions (lower-cost model) instead.
- Audit/permissions: who can set hard limits? (Proposition: only admins + owners of the tenant).

Backlog (groomed) — prioritized and estimated (T-shirt S/M/L):
1) Build compact card component + list API (M) — estimate: size M — owners: frontend (Leila) + API (Ethan) — linear UX-412
2) Expanded panel with sparkline + top-3 routes (M) — estimate: size M — depends on metrics service latency — linear UX-413
3) Throttle controls (soft-limit persistence + audit log) (M) — estimate: size S — include server-side validation — jira RED-1289
4) Route impact badges (S) — estimate: size S — small augmentation of routes table UX-414
5) CSV export & date-range filter (S) — estimate: size S — product asks for finance use-case
6) Burst allowance (time-limited override) UI & backend (L) — estimate: size L — policy review required
7) Per-route hard limits (B) — estimate: size L — requires policy + enforcement design
8) Anomaly linking: show detected spike + ‘view trace’ (integration with observability) (S) — estimate: size M
9) Accessibility pass + i18n prep (S) — estimate: size S

Notes from grooming meeting (2025-02-18):
- SRE asked for a quick ‘snooze alert’ action on the card for noisy keys — add as a follow-up (UX-420).
- Billing asked for a column that shows costs in USD estimated for the period (pricing model v1) — added to CSV scope.
- Devs requested an in-card quick-swap to route all traffic to ‘fallback-model’ — out of scope for MVP, capture in roadmap.

Quality metrics (post-launch to evaluate success):
- Time-to-detect: median time for keys crossing 80% quota to being acknowledged in console (target < 30m).
- Reduction in billing surprises: % decrease in support tickets labeled ‘unexpected bill’ tied to quota visibility (target 30% reduction in 90d).
- Engagement: % of keys with expanded panel opened at least once per month (target 20%).

Implementation notes for engineering handoff:
- Frontend: card should be a reusable component (props: consumableMetrics[]). Keep CSS at design token sizes to adapt to Console’s responsive grid.
- Backend: add aggregatedKeyUsage endpoint: /v1/keys/usage?ids=[...]&window=30d that returns small payload per key. Cache at 1m granularity for hot lists.
- Observability links should be pre-signed URLs to trace viewer; present as external link target=_blank.

Next steps / immediate action items:
- UX: produce high-fidelity mocks for desktop and mobile (Leila) — due 2025-03-03
- API: draft contract for aggregatedKeyUsage endpoint and pagination (Ethan) — due 2025-02-27
- PM: confirm quota window default (calendar-month) with Finance + Legal (Priya) — done: calendar-month, allow toggle

Misc notes and brainstorm fragments (raw):
- Consider a ‘heatmap’ mini for the top 10 routes inside the details pane for larger accounts.
- Potential future: allow rules like ‘if key X uses > 70% of quota AND route /image generates > 50% cost, auto-schedule model fallback’.
- UX curiosity: what if we show predicted end-of-month usage in the ring (dashed overlay)? Could help forecasting.

If you’re reviewing: please leave comments inline in the Figma mock or add notes in Linear UX-412.
